title: Never Enough Left at the End
gist_ar: برنامج نصايح مالية: المشكلة مش في الحاجات الكبيرة، المشكلة في الصغيرة اللي محدش بيحسبها.

before_listening.en: A radio money-advice programme with a caller. Listen for the host's MAIN advice, not the three steps.
before_listening.ar: برنامج نصايح مالية مع متصل. ركّز على النصيحة الأساسية، مش الخطوات التلاتة.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Our next caller has a problem that a lot of you wrote to us about. Go ahead, Kamal.

segments.speaker: Kamal
segments.text: I earn enough, I think, but there is never enough left at the end of the month. Both my sisters say I spend too much on small things, and neither of them is wrong. But I cannot see where it goes.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That is the most common problem we get, and it is almost never the big things. Try this for one month. Write down every amount under fifty pounds, and only those. Most people track the rent and forget the rest, and the rest is usually too big to ignore. Second: you said you earn enough. Enough for what? If you have no number, any amount feels too little. Pick one goal, one figure and one date. Third, and this is the hard one: neither saving nor earning more will help if you do not know the shape of the month. Some weeks are far more expensive than others. Find the expensive week, and move something out of it.

segments.speaker: Kamal
segments.text: The expensive week is always the first one.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Then you have just done the hardest part.

gist_question.q: What is the host's main advice?
options: Find a second job and earn more
Track the small spending and learn the shape of the month
Let his sisters manage his money for him

questions.q: Which amounts does she tell him to write down?
options: Only the rent and the bills

questions.q: Why does she ask 'enough for what?'
options: Because without a number, any amount feels too little
Because she thinks he does not earn enough
Because his sisters disagree with him

questions.q: What does Kamal realise at the end?
options: He spends too much on his sisters
The first week of the month is always the expensive one
He needs to move to a cheaper flat
